land.text: Nubia from the First Cataract to upstream of the Fourth, annexed by Egypt "c. 1504 BC"

successors.note: Thutmose I (reign 1505-1493 BC) cut the Tombos stele in his year 2 (1504 BC) and killed the Nubian king; the later Kingdom of Kush "emerged, possibly from Kerma" by the 11th century BC (Kerma culture page) and has its own dossier (kingdom-of-kush).

capitals.name: Kerma
capitals.note: Capital of the kingdom: the page says the culture was "centered in Kerma, Sudan, in ancient Nubia".

correction.text: the Dongola Reach around Kerma: "based in the southern part of Nubia, or Upper Nubia"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks Kerma). Early Kerma (2500-2000 BC) and Middle Kerma (2000-1750 BC): the page gives the seat and "Upper Nubia" but no boundary, so a 200 km radius around Kerma stands in; the page has no infobox area to compare. Egyptian Middle Kingdom forts lay to the north ("Senwosret I established forts at Ikkur, Quban, Aniba, Buhen, and Kor").

correction.text: "It controlled the 1st to 4th Cataracts" (Classic Kerma): the Nile from the First Cataract to upstream of the Fourth

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Classic Kerma (1750-1500 BC): "It controlled the 1st to 4th Cataracts". The page gives no boundary or area (the city is "about 25 hectares"); the Lower Nubia region plus a 250 km radius at Kerma approximates the Nile reach. Held to 1504 BC, the year the page gives for the Egyptian annexation.

ledger.note: c. 2500 BC: the kingdom of Kerma develops at Kerma in Upper Nubia. "developed from around 2500 BC, reaching its peak between 1750 BC and 1500 BC"; the infobox says established c. 2500 BC; Pre-Kerma had developed "between 3500 BC and 2500 BC in Upper Nubia".

region.text: the Dongola Reach around Kerma: "based in the southern part of Nubia, or Upper Nubia"

ledger.note: c. 1750 BC: Classic Kerma holds the Nile from the First Cataract. The page dates the Classic phase (1750-1500 BC) and the span of control but not the takeover of Lower Nubia from the Egyptian forts (Middle Kingdom, c. 1990-1725 BC): page silent on the year.

region.text: Lower Nubia from the First Cataract, which Classic Kerma controlled: "It controlled the 1st to 4th Cataracts"

ledger.note: 1575 BC: Kerma invades deep into Egypt, in partnership with the Hyksos. "Kerma invaded deep into Egypt between 1575 and 1550 BC"; the Kamose page adds that Apophis asked the king of Kush for aid against Kamose. The page names no ground, so the zone (Lower Nubia and the Aswan frontier) is my reading.

region.text: Kerma "invaded deep into Egypt between 1575 and 1550 BC"; the Nubians recaptured the fortress of Buhen from Kamose

ledger.note: 1549 BC: Kamose, last Theban king to campaign against Kush, is dated 1554-1549 BC (Ryholt); the page says "Kamose is known to have campaigned against the Kushites prior to his third year" and again in year 4 or 5, and that the Nubians had recaptured Buhen. How the fighting ended is not on the page: bridging date.

region.text: the Lower Nubian frontier fought over by Kamose and the king of Kush

ledger.note: c. 1504 BC: Egypt annexes Kerma and Nubia. "the Egyptian annexation of Nubia (Kerma/ Kush) c. 1504 BC"; the Thutmose I page puts his Tombos stele (a fortress "near the third cataract") in his year 2 and says his reign "effectively ended Nubian independence for around 500 years"; Kerma rebellions "continued for 220 years (till c. 1300 BC)".

region.text: Nubia from the First Cataract to upstream of the Fourth, annexed by Egypt

ledger.note: c. 1504 BC: the Kingdom of Kerma ends in the Egyptian annexation; a viceroy of Kush (Turi) is appointed by Thutmose I (Thutmose I page).

region.text: Kerma and its Nile reach, absorbed into the New Kingdom

wars.name: Kerma-Hyksos war against Thebes

zones.text: Lower Nubia and the Aswan frontier, Buhen recaptured by the Nubians

wars.outcome: Not settled on the pages: the Nubians recaptured Buhen from Kamose, who campaigned against the Kushites before his year 3 and again in year 4 or 5; Egyptian control of Nubia was re-established later.
wars.note: "Kerma invaded deep into Egypt between 1575 and 1550 BC" (Kerma culture page); the Kamose page dates only his year 3 and gives his reign as 1554-1549 BC.

wars.name: Thutmose I's Nubian campaigns

zones.text: Nubia to the Third Cataract (Tombos) and beyond to Kurgus

wars.outcome: Egyptian victory: the Nubian king killed in battle, a fortress built at Tombos, a viceroy of Kush appointed; Nubian independence ended for around 500 years.
wars.note: Years 2, 3 and 4 of a reign dated 1505-1493 BC give 1504-1502; the page records a rebellion in year 4. An inscription of his reign has been found as far south as Kurgus, south of the Fourth Cataract.

certainty.note: No source gives Kerma a boundary: the Egyptian frontier at the First Cataract (Middle Kingdom forts to c. 1725 BC) and the Fourth Cataract are the only limits named.

sources.title: Kerma culture
sources.note: Identity, phases (Early 2500-2000, Middle 2000-1750, Classic 1750-1500), territory (1st to 4th Cataract), Egyptian invasion 1575-1550, annexation c. 1504. No infobox area.

sources.title: Kamose
sources.note: Year 3 stela: Apophis asks the king of Kush for aid; Kamose campaigns against Kush before year 3 and again in year 4 or 5; Buhen recaptured by the Nubians; reign 1554-1549 BC.

sources.title: Thutmose I
sources.note: Nubian rebellion and campaigns in years 2-4 (Tombos fortress, Kurgus inscription), end of Nubian independence for about 500 years, viceroy of Kush; reign 1505-1493 BC.

notes:
New state, Cliopatria has no Kerma row (the Kingdom of Kush row starts in -1000). Pages opened: Kerma culture, Kamose, Thutmose I (3 of the 2-5 budget). Wikidata id left null because wikidata.org is unreachable and the id is not on any opened page.
Unsettled: when Kerma took Lower Nubia from the Egyptian forts (the page gives the forts' span as c. 1990-1725 BC and the Classic phase 1750-1500, not the takeover), how the Kerma-Hyksos war ended, and the Egyptian reconquest between Kamose and Thutmose I (Ahmose I and Amenhotep I are not on the pages opened; Thutmose I's page says Nubia 'rebelled' at his coronation, which implies earlier Egyptian rule). A gap-filler should open Ahmose I and the Nubia page. The Kerma culture page has no km2 figure, so no area comparison is possible; the keyframes are radius approximations around Kerma.
Counterparts: seventeenth-dynasty-of-egypt, hyksos, new-kingdom-of-egypt (all Cliopatria rows, other groups). The Kingdom of Kush (kingdom-of-kush, Cliopatria row from -1000) is the later state 'possibly from Kerma'; the 500-year gap -1500 to -1000 is Egyptian rule (Wawat, Kush viceroyalty), not covered here.
